meta.title: tezera Platform Architecture (ATP release, serverless on AWS Amplify)
meta.subtitle: Mobile app and web portal for organisers, providers and consumers

boundaries.label: AWS · ap-south-1 (Mumbai) · Amplify Gen 2 backend, serverless

cards.title: Where it runs: why, and alternatives
items: AWS Amplify Gen 2 (backend). Why: the whole backend (auth, data, storage, functions) is defined in TypeScript in the repository and deployed by Amplify through AWS CDK; each developer gets a personal cloud sandbox, and each Git branch can get its own backend. Everything is serverless, so nothing sleeps or needs a server kept running. Alternatives: Firebase, Supabase, or the earlier design (NestJS on Render with Neon and Upstash).

Amplify Hosting (web portal). Why: builds and serves the Next.js portal, including server-rendered pages, from the same Git repository as the backend, with a preview link per pull request. Alternatives: Vercel, Netlify.

Region ap-south-1 (Mumbai). Why: the nearest AWS region to Sri Lanka. Watch: personal data is stored outside Sri Lanka, so check the PDPA's rules on cross-border transfers before launch (not checked).

Cost. Lambda, DynamoDB, SQS, Cognito and S3 have free monthly allowances, and AWS changed its free tier for new accounts in July 2025 (credits instead of 12 months free). Check the current terms and set an AWS Budgets alert before the pilot (limits not verified).

cards.title: Services and protocols: why, and alternatives
items: GraphQL with AppSync subscriptions instead of REST + SSE. Why: Amplify Data generates a typed client for the app and the portal from one schema, applies per-role auth rules, and pushes live updates (chat, event status, 'Going' counts) over WebSockets that AWS manages. One deliberate exception: a Lambda function URL that only receives PayHere payment notifications. Alternatives: REST on API Gateway + Lambda with API Gateway WebSockets.

Amazon Cognito (Amplify Auth). Why: sign-up with email or phone, one Cognito group per role (organiser, vendor, freelancer, consumer, admin) that the auth rules check. A custom SMS sender Lambda sends sign-in codes through Dialog e-SMS instead of Amazon SNS.

Expo Push. Why: one push API over FCM and APNs for the React Native app, called from Lambda. Amazon Pinpoint push is not used: AWS ends its support on 30 October 2026. Alternatives: Amazon SNS mobile push, OneSignal.
Amazon SES (email). Why: inside AWS and cheap per message. Watch: new accounts start in the SES sandbox; request production access before the pilot. Alternatives: Resend, Brevo.

Dialog e-SMS (OTP and urgent alerts). Why: a Sri Lankan operator's gateway with sender ID masking and billing in LKR. Watch: needs a Dialog Enterprise account and its API documentation is thin, so test early. Alternatives: Amazon SNS SMS, Notify.lk.

Amazon Bedrock with Claude (AI map draft, Could). Why: stays inside AWS, uses IAM, no separate API key. Watch: Claude on Bedrock in ap-south-1 is not verified; it may need cross-region inference. Alternatives: the Anthropic API directly.

cards.title: Recommended stack
items: One TypeScript monorepo with the Amplify Gen 2 backend (amplify/ folder) beside the app and the portal
Mobile: React Native + Expo with the Amplify JavaScript libraries; one app for all four roles
Web: Next.js portal on Amplify Hosting for every role, consumers included, plus a role-gated admin panel
Data: Amplify Data schema in TypeScript, served by AppSync and stored in DynamoDB; custom logic in Lambda functions
Jobs: SQS queue and EventBridge Scheduler trigger Lambda functions; DynamoDB Streams trigger reranking; a Lambda function URL takes PayHere payment notifications

cards.title: Venue map builder and interactive 2D map
items: Map builder on the web portal: organisers draw, move, resize, label and delete zones, stalls and pins over a background, with grid snapping, undo and a scale set from two marked points; the mobile app does quick on-the-day edits (move, rename, hide)
Three ways to start: a PNG/JPG or PDF floor plan (a Lambda turns the PDF's first page into the background image), a blank grid of a set size, or a saved venue map

Every map, however it starts, is saved in one standard, versioned map JSON: background, scale, and zones, stalls and pins as boxes or points in 0–1 coordinates with stable IDs; each publish is a new version and an earlier one can be restored

AI draft (Could): a Lambda sends the floor plan image to Claude on Amazon Bedrock and gets draft zones and stalls back; it opens as an editable draft, nothing publishes until the organiser checks it, and text in the image is treated as data. Claude in ap-south-1 not verified (may need cross-region inference)
Concept and code reused from Damian's own ai-studio repo (image to editable draft, click to edit, a new revision per save), adapted to Amplify rather than lifted whole
Consumers tap a zone to see its stalls; each stall shows the vendor, items and prices in LKR
Search by item (e.g. 'kottu') highlights matching stalls; 'Find on map' jumps to a stall
Map JSON versions in DynamoDB, background images in S3 (split proposed); drawn as an SVG overlay: react-native-svg in the app, SVG in Next.js
Mobile app only: keeps an opened event's map, times and announcements offline, with a 'last updated' time (Could)

cards.title: Sandboxed payments (Should)
items: Sandbox only in the ATP: PayHere test mode, no real money moves; every payment screen and receipt says 'Test payment, no real money'
Direct to the payee: each provider (and each organiser, for stall fees) connects their own PayHere merchant account; the web portal opens its hosted checkout and the app uses the PayHere mobile SDK

Tezera never holds, splits or pays out funds. Holding or splitting money would most likely need CBSL registration as a money or value transfer service (LKR 15m capital), so this design also works for a real launch (not legal advice)
Covers booking deposits and instalments, stall fees, and cancellation fees and refunds per the booking's terms; Tezera's commission is a separate receipt line (rate proposed, not charged in the ATP)
PayHere sits behind a small payment-provider adapter, so Genie Business or WEBXPAY can be added later

The Payments Lambda behind a function URL checks PayHere's signature, ignores repeats of an order ID, and writes the payment to DynamoDB, which marks the instalment received; merchant secrets stay server-side (Secrets Manager or encrypted, proposed)
Card details are entered only on PayHere's page (PCI DSS SAQ A scope); a payee with no connected account is paid outside the app and the instalment is marked received by hand

cards.title: Data models (Amplify Data)
items: Accounts, profiles and verification
Events and promotion feed (posts, reels)
Hiring marketplace: direct bookings, job posts, quotes, payment terms, stalls
Payments (sandbox): connected accounts, payments, refunds, receipts
Reviews and ranking (weighted rank score, badges, leaderboards)
Venue maps: versioned map JSON, saved venue maps, stall items and prices
Community boards, meetups, messaging, announcements
Admin: verification, report queue, disputes, audit log

cards.title: Data design on DynamoDB (replaces the PostgreSQL design)
items: Rank score: an attribute on each profile, recalculated by a Lambda when a review is written or hidden (DynamoDB Streams)
Leaderboards: a GSI keyed by category#district and sorted by rank score; top N is one query
Feed: built on read from each followed organiser's posts (GSI by author and date), merged, with cursor pagination; organisers are few
Trending: a scheduled Lambda scores recent posts and stores the top list (score proposed)
Likes as their own items (post + user), so no double likes; like and view counts kept with atomic counters
Search: GSIs for category, district and date plus name prefix match; Algolia or Typesense later if the pilot needs typo-tolerant search
Tools: NoSQL Workbench to model tables and access patterns; Amplify sandbox for test data

cards.title: Reviews and trust
items: Organiser and provider reviews unlock on a completed booking or a confirmed stall
Attendee reviews unlock from a 'Going' mark made before the event, once it ends
EventBridge Scheduler closes review windows after 14 days; a Lambda recomputes rank scores
Verification documents sit in a private S3 path that only the admin group can read, through short-lived links (PDPA)

cards.title: Out of scope
items: Ticketing: tiers, seats, RSVP tickets, QR entry, ticket refunds
Real money: the ATP uses the PayHere sandbox only
Google Maps directions to the venue: still under discussion
